recent_events.title: The Canadian Press wins National Newspaper Award for Ring of Fire coverage
recent_events.description: CP journalists Liam Casey and Christopher Katsarov Luna won the National Newspaper Award for their extensive coverage from the Ring of Fire region in Northern Ontario, highlighting the landscape, the people and the powerful politics at play. CP received seven NNA nominations in total for 2025.
recent_events.impact: Reinforces CP's reputation for investigative journalism and strengthens its competitive position in Canadian media awards

recent_events.title: Trump's tariff war voted CP News Story of the Year for 2025
recent_events.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's tariff campaign against Canada and the surge in patriotic zeal it inspired were voted The Canadian Press News Story of the Year. Nearly two-thirds of editors and news directors across the country picked the tariff war as the most consequential story of 2025.
recent_events.impact: Highlights CP's annual editorial survey as a barometer of Canadian national news priorities and its role in framing public discourse

recent_events.title: Mark Carney named CP Newsmaker of the Year for 2025
recent_events.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney was selected as The Canadian Press Newsmaker of the Year in an annual survey of newsroom editors and leaders. Carney's swift transformation from a relatively low-profile public figure to a dominant presence in Canadian politics made him an unmistakable choice.
recent_events.impact: Annual Newsmaker selection reinforces CP's editorial authority in Canadian journalism

recent_events.title: Ontario court clears Canadian news publishers' copyright lawsuit against OpenAI to proceed
recent_events.description: An Ontario Superior Court judge ruled that the copyright lawsuit filed by a coalition of Canadian media organizations including The Canadian Press, Torstar, The Globe and Mail, Postmedia and CBC/Radio-Canada against OpenAI can proceed in Canada. The coalition alleges OpenAI used their news content to train ChatGPT without permission or compensation.
recent_events.impact: Landmark case for AI and copyright in Canadian media, with significant implications for news content protection and AI regulation

recent_events.title: CP covers Prime Minister Carney's first Asia trip for ASEAN and APEC summits
recent_events.description: The Canadian Press provided extensive coverage of Prime Minister Mark Carney's first trip to Asia, attending ASEAN and APEC summits in Malaysia and South Korea. CP reported on Carney's meeting with Xi Jinping on the sidelines of APEC and Canada's efforts to deepen trade relationships in the Indo-Pacific region.
recent_events.impact: Demonstrates CP's role as primary wire service for Canadian international affairs coverage, including APEC-related stories

recent_events.title: OpenAI argues Canadian publishers' lawsuit should be heard in U.S.
recent_events.description: OpenAI appeared in Ontario court to argue that the copyright lawsuit brought by Canadian news publishers including The Canadian Press should be heard in a U.S. courtroom rather than Canada. The coalition argued the case belongs in Canadian courts.
recent_events.impact: Jurisdictional dispute with implications for how international AI companies can be held accountable under Canadian law

recent_events.title: CP develops cautious AI policy for newsroom use
recent_events.description: Editor-in-chief Andrea Baillie described months of careful policy development for AI use in the CP newsroom, aligned with partners. CP established guidelines ensuring any information sourced from AI must be verified. The policy emphasizes accuracy, honesty and fairness as bedrock principles.
recent_events.impact: Positions CP as a responsible leader in AI adoption among Canadian newsrooms, balancing innovation with editorial integrity

core_business: 加拿大通讯社（The Canadian Press，简称CP/加通社）是加拿大的国家通讯社，成立于1917年，总部位于多伦多阿德莱德东街60号。加通社是加拿大历史最悠久的新闻机构之一，最初由国会法案设立为报纸新闻合作社，2010年转型为营利性企业，由加拿大三家主要媒体集团——Torstar（多伦多星报母公司）、环球邮报（The Globe and Mail）和Square Victoria Communications Group（蒙特利尔新闻报La Presse母公司）共同持股。加通社的核心业务包括：一是新闻通讯服务，拥有超过180名记者编辑，分布在多伦多、渥太华、蒙特利尔、温哥华、埃德蒙顿、哈利法克斯等七个分社和卡尔加里、里贾纳、温尼伯、维多利亚、圣约翰斯、弗雷德里克顿及华盛顿特区等七个办事处，以英语和法语双语向加拿大几乎所有日报、广播电台、电视台和新闻网站提供文字、图片、音频、视频及图表内容；二是图片档案服务，运营加拿大最大的在线新闻图片编辑档案库，收录超过200万张数字图片，自1996年建成以来为加拿大首家；三是出版服务，出版《CP Stylebook》和《Caps and Spelling》，被视为加拿大新闻工作者、公关专业人士和编辑的标准写作指南；四是公关分发服务，通过与Nasdaq GlobeNewswire的独家合作，向CP通讯网络分发新闻稿。加通社与美联社（AP）保持长期独家合作关系，AP为CP在加拿大境内的独家国际新闻供应商，CP则为AP在美加地区以外的独家加拿大新闻分销商。在总编辑安德烈娅·贝利（Andrea Baillie）领导下，加通社近年来积极应对AI技术挑战，制定了审慎的新闻室AI使用政策，并与其他加拿大主要媒体机构联合起诉OpenAI侵犯版权。
apec_stance: 加拿大通讯社作为国家通讯社，虽不直接参与APEC政策制定，但在APEC相关新闻报道中发挥核心作用。加通社是加拿大主流媒体关于APEC峰会、亚太贸易关系和印太战略的主要新闻来源。2025年10月，加通社对加拿大总理卡尼首次亚洲之行及APEC韩国峰会进行了全面报道，包括卡尼与习近平在APEC峰会期间的会晤、加拿大深化印太贸易关系的努力以及加拿大与东盟的合作。加通社的年度新闻人物评选和年度新闻评选机制也反映了亚太事务在加拿大公共议程中的重要性——特朗普关税战被选为2025年度新闻，凸显了国际贸易摩擦对加拿大的深远影响。作为美联社（AP）在加拿大的独家分销商，加通社间接参与了全球新闻在APEC区域的流通。加通社与其他加拿大媒体联合对OpenAI提起的版权诉讼也具有APEC维度的意义，涉及AI训练数据的跨境使用和知识产权保护问题。
